name: anti_boatmurdered
content:
# ABM Seam — Full Plan (Ghost wave-2)

## 0. Thesis

You cannot make userspace trustworthy against `SIGKILL`, power loss, or panics. So the seam does exactly one thing well: **it moves as much footprint as possible into kernel-reclaimed constructs, and everything that can't be kernel-reclaimed becomes a leased, journaled, namespace-exclusive artifact with a bounded staleness window.** Residue is never "discovered by the operator"; it is either impossible, self-expiring, or reported by us before they find it.

Three load-bearing rules:

- **INV-1 (Tiering):** every footprint item is classified Tier 0 (kernel-reclaimed), Tier 1 (leased/auto-reaped), or Tier 2 (persistent-by-design, declared). Nothing exists outside a tier.
- **INV-2 (Namespace exclusivity):** everything we create lives inside reserved namespaces we provably solely own (`/var/lib/ghost/**`, cgroup `ghost.slice`, nft table `ghost_*`, bpf pin dir `/sys/fs/bpf/ghost/<inst>/**`, device names `gh*`, contracted port ranges). Anything found inside our namespace is ours by construction → safe to reap after grace. This kills the ambiguity problem that makes janitors dangerous.
- **INV-3 (Single entry point):** no acquisition of any footprint item happens except through `registrar`. Enforced by lint/import-ban, admission gate, and runtime audit in dev builds.

---

## 1. Footprint taxonomy

**Tier 0 — kernel-reclaimed (prefer these; zero work needed even on `-9`):**
threads, fds, memfd, pipes, abstract unix sockets, memory mappings, children confined to `ghost.slice` sub-cgroups (die when the slice is removed), Windows Job Object children (`KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE`), Linux `PR_SET_PDEATHSIG` children. Policy: new footprint types must justify why they aren't Tier 0.

**Tier 1 — leased (auto-reclaimed; bounded staleness):**
named files/tempdirs, POSIX shm/sems, filesystem unix sockets, pidfiles, bound ports, TUN/TAP devices, pinned eBPF progs/maps, nftables tables, mounts + loop devices inside state root, file locks, distributed locks. Each carries a lease (TTL ≤ 60 s, heartbeat ≤ 20 s) and a journal entry. Max residue lifetime after unclean death: **TTL + janitor interval ≤ 90 s**, and **0 s on any graceful path**.

**Tier 2 — persistent-by-design:**
config, state DB, logs, user data. Declared in contract, versioned, removable only via explicit `ghost uninstall --purge`. Never created implicitly; creating an undeclared Tier-2 item is a policy violation, not a bug.

---

## 2. Architecture — six modules

```
┌────────────────────────── ghost runtime ──────────────────────────┐
│  components ──call──> registrar ──write-ahead──> ledger (WAL)     │
│                          │                                        │
│                          ├──> guards (RAII handles, LIFO drop)    │
│                          └──> kernel objects (Tier 0/1)           │
│                                                                   │
│  probes (read-only ground truth, per OS/class)                    │
│  reaper (lease expiry + pdeathsig escalation, periodic)           │
│  janitor (boot-time + periodic reconciliation: ledger ⇄ probes)   │
│  receipt writer (end-of-shutdown proof artifact)                  │
└───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
          ▲                                   │
          └──── supervisor (own death also triggers kernel reclaim;
                watchdog: stall > 500 ms in crit section ⇒ dump+abort;
                heartbeat lost ⇒ SIGABRT → cgroup kill → next-boot janitor)
```

### Interfaces (concrete)

```rust
trait Registrar {
    fn acquire(&self, tok: CapabilityToken, req: AcquireReq) -> Result<Guard, AcquireErr>;
    // AcquireReq { kind: Kind, key: CanonicalKey, contract_ref: LineId }
    // Refuses if: no contract_ref, contract quota exceeded, key outside reserved namespace,
    //             policy engine denies kind for this component.
}

trait Guard: Send {
    fn release(self);                 // explicit; also impl Drop => release()
    fn lease(&self) -> &LeaseHandle;  // heartbeat handle; drop stops heartbeats
    fn info(&self) -> FootprintInfo;  // feeds introspection
}

trait Probe {                           // one impl per (os, class)
    fn class(&self) -> Class;
    fn scan(&self) -> Vec<LiveItem>;    // LiveItem { key, owner_evidence, born_at }
}   // classes: ProcGroup, FdSet, Port, TmpFile, Shm, Sem, UnixSock,
    //         BpfPin, NftTable, Tun, Mount, LoopDev, DistLock, FileLock

fn janitor_reconcile(live: &[LiveItem], ledger: &Ledger) -> Vec<Action>;
// Action ∈ { MarkReleased, Reap, Quarantine, FlagDrift }  — deterministic (INV-9)

fn write_receipt(r: ShutdownReceipt) -> io::Result<PathBuf>;
```

Identity rule (kills PID-reuse bugs): a live process is identified by `(boot_id, pgid, /proc/<pid>/stat field 22 start_time, exe-hash)` — never PID alone.

---

## 3. Ledger

Append-only WAL, `O_DSYNC` writes + directory fsync, hash-chained records (tamper-evident audit trail — this is the code-as-law evidence layer):

```
Acquire  { seq, ts, actor: component@boot_id@inst_uuid, kind, key,
           lease_ttl_ms, contract_ref, prev_hash, hash }
Release  { seq, ts, acq_seq, how: EXPLICIT | DROP | REAPED | GHOST }
Incident { seq, ts, kind: DRIFT | SHUTDOWN_INCOMPLETE | QUARANTINE, payload }
```

- Written **before** acquisition (write-ahead). If the process dies between journal and acquire, janitor sees an unreferenced lease and cleans conservatively.
- Disk-full during write ⇒ fail closed: refuse the acquisition. Over-cleaning inside our exclusive namespace is always safe; under-cleaning is not.
- Compaction on clean shutdown: replay releases, keep only open leases + last-N incidents.

---

## 4. Shutdown choreography (graceful path)

Global budgets: **soft 10 s, hard 30 s**. Phases, each with its own deadline; overrun escalates to the next phase, never blocks:

1. **Quiesce (≤ 2 s):** stop admission, cancel accepted-but-unstarted work, broadcast cancel tokens.
2. **Drain (≤ 4 s):** in-flight tasks finish or checkpoint. Unfinished ⇒ checkpointed + journaled, not lost silently.
3. **Release (≤ 2 s):** guards dropped in strict reverse-acquisition order (LIFO — dependency correctness: unmount before deleting backing file, close TUN before removing nft rules that steer to it).
4. **Reap (≤ 2 s):** kill process groups: SIGTERM → 500 ms → SIGCONT+SIGKILL (SIGCONT because SIGSTOP'd processes don't service SIGKILL delivery until continued). `waitpid` with WaitDelay; zombie reaper thread owns all waits.
5. **Verify (≤ 200 ms):** run all probes, diff vs ledger.
   - Empty ⇒ write `ShutdownReceipt{boot_id, ts, ledger_final_hash, probes_all_empty: true, duration_ms, anomalies: []}`.
   - Non-empty ⇒ run janitor once inline, rewrite receipt with `anomalies` populated, file Incident. **Never hang**: at hard deadline the supervisor SIGKILLs `ghost.slice`; kernel does Tier-0 reclamation; next boot's janitor finishes Tier-1. The operator sees a receipt-or-incident, never silence.

Interrupt path (Ctrl-C): identical, entered immediately, must reach quiescence ≤ 2 s, emits `InterruptedRecord`.

---

## 5. Anti-wedge discipline (the "blocking calls" half of boatmurdered)

- **Every operator-invoked command has a declared deadline** (default 5 s). On expiry: print partial state, exit code `3 = PARTIAL`. Long operations become tickets: submit → poll → fetch result. There is no verb in the CLI that can hang.
- **No unbounded blocking anywhere on control paths:** connect/send/recv timeouts mandatory; locking is trylock-with-deadline; no network FS on control path or state root (stale NFS handles are textbook boatmurder — forbidden by contract).
- **No IO under internal locks.** Global lock-order registry; lint-enforced.
- **Critical-section watchdog:** any section > 500 ms ⇒ stack dump + SIGABRT (core retained) — fail-stop beats wedged.
- **Main-loop heartbeat** to supervisor; missed beats escalate dump → abort → cgroup kill.
- **Transactional apply for any mutating operation:** stage → commit → verify → auto-rollback journal on failure. No half-applied states left behind.

---

## 6. Janitor reconciliation

Runs at boot (mandatory, before serving traffic) and every 30 s thereafter.

```
live   = ⋃ probes.scan()
open   = ledger.open_leases()

owned ∩ live ∧ (lease.expired ∨ issuer.boot_id ≠ current)  → REAP (destroy + Release{REAPED})
owned − live                                               → MarkReleased(GHOST)
live − owned (inside our namespaces)                        → observe twice across scans,
                                                             then REAP (exclusive-namespace safety)
live − owned (outside our namespaces)                       → FlagDrift + Incident; NEVER touch.
                                                             Quarantine only if inside a quarantinable
                                                             class; alert with full evidence bundle.
```

Determinism requirement (INV-9): same journal + same probe output ⇒ same actions. Property-tested with 10k fuzz cases. Drift outside our namespace is reported, never destroyed — operator trust is part of the footprint.

---

## 7. Failure matrix

| Trigger | Mechanism | Residual window |
|---|---|---|
| Graceful stop | Choreography §4 + receipt | 0 s |
| `SIGKILL` whole tree | Tier-0 kernel reclaim + leases expire + janitor | ≤ 90 s |
| Power loss / VM kill | Same as above (journal survives; boot_id mismatch drives reap) | ≤ 90 s |
| Panic / watchdog abort | Same as SIGKILL path + core + Incident pre-written | ≤ 90 s |
| Child escapes and forks | cgroup `pids.max` + subreaper; slice removal kills tree | ≤ 90 s |
| Disk full during journal | Fail-closed acquire; namespace-exclusive over-clean allowed | 0 s added |
| Clock skew on leases | Wallclock + monotonic dual stamps; dist locks arbitrated by store clock | — |
| Unknown artifact in our namespace | Double-observation reap (§6) | ≤ 2 scan intervals |
| Artifact outside namespace | Drift report only; human decides | reported immediately |
| Supervisor itself dies | Its parent (init/unit) removes `ghost.slice` ⇒ Tier-0 collapse; leases lapse | ≤ 90 s |

---

## 8. Footprint Contract (governance layer)

Declarative, versioned, per-component; admission control refuses to boot a component without a valid contract, and `registrar` refuses any acquire whose `contract_ref` doesn't resolve:

```yaml
contract: v1
component: scheduler
process_groups: { max: 4, pattern: "gh-sched-*", cgroup: "ghost.slice/sched" }
ports: [{ proto: tcp, range: [21000, 21100] }]
tmp: { root: "/var/lib/ghost/tmp/scheduler", bytes: 1GiB }
kernel:
  bpf:      { pin_dir: "/sys/fs/bpf/ghost/scheduler", max_progs: 8 }
  nft_tables: ["ghost_sched"]
  tun:      { max: 2, pattern: "gh0-sched-*" }
budgets_ms: { shutdown_soft: 10000, shutdown_hard: 30000, cmd_default: 5000 }
forbidden: [cron, systemd_units, mounts_outside_state_root, nfs_on_control_path, setuid]
tier2_persistent: ["/var/lib/ghost/state/scheduler.db"]
```

Enforcement stack (code-as-law):

1. **Static:** import/type ban on raw spawn/open/socket/bpf/mount constructors outside `registrar` (compiler plugin / lint rule set, wired into merge gate). A PR adding a direct acquisition call site cannot pass CI.
2. **Admission:** contract validated against cluster policy (quotas, namespace patterns) at load; violations block boot with a precise diagnostic.
3. **Runtime (dev/staging builds):** seccomp-notify auditor flags any footprint-class syscall whose fd/arg isn't backed by an open lease — catches gaps static analysis misses.
4. **Audit:** the ledger's hash chain is the immutable who/what/when record; `ghost footprint verify --audit` replays and verifies chain integrity.

---

## 9. Verification (this is where anti-boatmurdered is proven, not claimed)

- **Kill-matrix harness:** extract every acquire↔release pair from coverage data; fault-inject (ptrace/seccomp-notify; QEMU pause+powercut for the paranoid tier) at every midpoint of every pair. Post-crash: run janitor, wait ≤ 90 s, assert all probes empty for Tier 0+1, assert ledger replay converges. Required coverage: ≥ 95% of boundary midpoints; violations block the release train.
- **Nightly chaos soak:** 8 h random kills under sustained load. SLO: **zero residue events past TTL**, zero unwitnessed drift. Any hit is a ship-blocker.
- **CI delta scan:** around every test run, snapshot `/proc`, fd tables, listening sockets, `/dev/shm`, bpf pins, nft, mounts, tmp roots — assert zero delta.
- **Property tests:** (a) reconciliation determinism (10k fuzz); (b) "∀ kill point p: reclaim(p) terminates ≤ 90 s ∧ footprint = ∅".
- **Wedging tests:** every CLI verb executed against a node with: dead store, full disk, blackholed peer, stopped child — assert exit ≤ deadline, code ∈ {0,1,3}, partial data printed.

---

## 10. Operator surface

```
ghost footprint ls [--all]          # live inventory: key, tier, owner, age, lease TTL, contract_ref
ghost footprint verify              # ledger ⇄ reality diff; exit 0 healthy; else machine-readable diff JSON
ghost footprint gc --dry-run|--yes  # manual janitor pass; dry-run default
ghost doctor                        # includes footprint audit + receipt history
ghost receipts ls|show <boot_id>    # shutdown proofs; missing receipt for non-graceful end + residue
                                    # found ⇒ incident auto-filed
```

Exit codes standardized: `0` ok · `1` error · `2` usage · `3` partial (deadline hit, partial data printed). No command hangs — ever.

---

## 11. Rollout (wave-2 internal integration)

- **2a — Shadow:** ledger+registrar+probes for ProcGroup/TmpFile/Port. Enforcement off; drift reports weekly against wave-1 components. Deliverable: first real-world residue census.
- **2b — Enforce-new:** admission gate ON for new code; migrate wave-1 components one per cycle; janitor active in staging; kill-matrix in CI (advisory → blocking at end of 2b).
- **2c — Full:** leases for BpfPin/NftTable/Tun/Mount/Shm/Sem/DistLock; receipts mandatory in prod; chaos soak gate ON; static acquisition-site ban blocking.
- **Exit criteria:** §9 suites green for two consecutive weeks; `footprint verify` exit 0 fleet-wide steady-state; zero Tier-1 residue incidents in prod for 30 days.

## 12. Invariant summary

1. INV-1 tiering — nothing exists outside Tier 0/1/2.
2. INV-2 namespace exclusivity — our namespaces, our garbage, reapable by construction.
3. INV-3 single entry point — all acquisition via `registrar`, statically gated.
4. INV-4 write-ahead — journal precedes acquire; fail closed on journal failure.
5. INV-5 bounded staleness — Tier-1 residue ≤ 90 s post-death, 0 s post-graceful.
6. INV-6 receipts — every shutdown ends in a receipt or a filed incident, never silence.
7. INV-7 no wedge — every operator path has a deadline and degrades to partial, never hangs.
8. INV-8 LIFO release — teardown order = reverse acquisition order, always.
9. INV-9 deterministic janitor — same inputs, same actions, property-proven.
10. INV-10 declared-only — undeclared footprint is a policy violation caught at three layers (static, admission, runtime audit), before it can become archaeology.

1. The anti-boatmurdered seam: a subsystem/boundary that guarantees clean shutdown, resource reclamation, no leaks.
2. The footprint contract: a formal contract specifying what footprint a component may leave on the host/system at any point (especially after crash/kill/shutdown).

This is a real design task. I should produce a thorough, concrete plan: architecture, interfaces, invariants, enforcement mechanisms, verification, failure matrices, rollout plan, telemetry, etc. Code-as-law governance suggests contracts enforced by code, maybe with policy-as-code checks.

Let me think about what "footprint" means:
- Processes spawned
- Threads
- File descriptors
- Sockets/listening ports
- Temp files/dirs
- Shared memory segments
- IPC handles (named pipes, unix sockets)
- Kernel objects (cgroups, namespaces, netns, mounts, loop devices, TAP devices, eBPF programs/maps, iptables/nftables rules, sysctls changed)

Anti-boatmurdered goals:
- At any moment, the live footprint is enumerable (introspection).
- On graceful stop: zero residue.
- On SIGKILL -9 / power loss / panic: residue is either (a) impossible, (b) auto-reclaimed on restart by a janitor pass, or (c) explicitly leased with TTL so it self-expires.
- No blocking calls that can wedge the operator's discovery tools: i.e., all control-plane operations are bounded-time; no unbounded waits; timeouts everywhere; watchdogs.
- Operator-facing "discovery" command: `ghost footprint` enumerates everything, compares against ledger, flags drift.

Design elements:

**Core concept: The Ledger.** Every kernel/resource acquisition goes through a registrar that writes an intent record (WAL/journal) before acquisition, and marks release after. Crash between acquire and release → journal shows pending lease → janitor reconciles.

**Leases/TTLs:** Every persistent footprint item carries a lease with heartbeat; if heartbeat dies, reaper collects. This handles SIGKILL.

**Ownership via cgroups/pdeathsig/process groups:** child processes spawned into dedicated cgroup or process group; parent death signal (PR_SET_PDEATHSIG) on Linux; on macOS use process groups + kqueue NOTE_EXIT monitoring; Windows Job Objects with JOB_OBJECT_LIMIT_KILL_ON_JOB_CLOSE.

**Kernel-object wrappers:** every kernel object type gets an owner token + destructor registered in a drop table; RAII-style guards; language-level enforcement (Rust Drop, defer in Go, etc.), plus finalizers as backstop with warnings.

**Blocking-call discipline:** no unbounded blocking on the control path. All blocking ops wrapped in deadline context; async runtime tasks tracked with cancellation tokens; shutdown sequence has global deadline; anything not done by deadline gets force-aborted and reported. Never hold a mutex while doing IO; never block the event loop thread; syscalls with timeouts (SO_SNDTIMEO etc.).

**Two-phase shutdown:** drain → revoke leases → reap children → destroy kernel objects → verify empty → emit receipt. Receipt is machine-checkable: hash of ledger state == empty.

**Janitor/sweeper:** on startup, reconcile journal vs. reality: enumerate actual processes (by pgid/cgroup), files (by tmpdir prefix), sockets (by SO_REUSEPORT? no — by bound ports recorded), eBPF pins, etc.; kill/orphan-clean anything owned but not heartbeated; report unexplained residue as drift.

**Footprint contract:** a typed manifest each component must declare statically (max processes, max fds, port ranges, tmpdir paths, kernel features used). Registrar enforces quotas. Contract versioned; CI tests assert no undeclared footprints (run under seccomp/audit to catch undeclared syscalls like bpf(), mount()).

**Verification/testing:**
- Kill-matrix tests: send SIGKILL at every syscall boundary (fault injection), then run janitor, then assert footprint == {} within TTL.
- Chaos harness: random kills at random times in soak; post-mortem scan.
- Leak detector in CI: run test suite, snapshot /proc, lsof, ss, bpftool, lsmod-ish diffs before/after; assert delta == 0.
- Property test: "for all kill points p: reclaim(p) terminates within T and yields empty footprint."

**Operator surface:**
- `ghost footprint ls` — live inventory with owners, ages, leases.
- `ghost footprint verify` — diff ledger vs reality; exit nonzero on drift.
- `ghost footprint gc` — forced sweep (with confirmation / dry-run default).
- `ghost doctor` — includes footprint audit.
- Everything non-blocking: commands have hard deadlines (e.g., 5s) and degrade to reporting partial state rather than hanging.

**Code-as-law governance integration:**
- Footprint contract expressed as policy (e.g., Rego/Cel or a custom schema); admission control refuses to start components whose manifests violate policy or lack contract.
- Every acquisition call site annotated with capability token derived from manifest; static analysis/lint enforces "no raw spawn/open without registrar."
- Audit log: append-only, tamper-evident (hash chain), who acquired/released what, when.

Now, structure the answer as the full concrete plan. The instruction says: reason thoroughly, then emit the full concrete plan as the final content. No fluff. So the output should be the plan itself, well-structured, dense, concrete: names of modules, interface signatures, data schemas, invariants numbered, failure matrix table, rollout phases, acceptance criteria.

Let me define naming:
- Seam name: maybe "the Reclaimer" or "ABM seam". Components:
  - `ledger` (journal): append-only WAL of acquisitions/releases with leases.
  - `registrar`: API through which all footprint acquisitions flow. Only legal entry point.
  - `guards`: RAII handles.
  - `janitor`: startup reconciliation + periodic reaper.
  - `reaper`: lease expiry enforcement.
  - `receipt`: end-of-shutdown proof artifact.
  - `contract`: declarative manifest schema + policy engine hooks.
  - `probe`: enumeration adapters per OS/kernel object class ("probes" read ground truth).

Ground-truth probes per class:
- processes: cgroup membership (Linux), pgid scan, job object (Windows).
- fds/sockets: /proc/self/fd, ss/lsof equivalents.
- tempfiles: managed tmp roots only (`$GHOST_STATE/tmp/<owner-uuid>/...`), never /tmp directly.
- shm/semaphores: /dev/shm prefix, POSIX named sems prefix `/.ghost-*`.
- network: bound ports recorded; TUN/TAP devices named `gh0-*`; nftables table `ghost_*`; eBPF pinned under `/sys/fs/bpf/ghost/<instance>/`.
- mounts: mount under instance dir with lazy umount fallback; loop devices attached to files inside state root.
- locks: flock on `$STATE/root.lock`; distributed locks with TTL in metadata store.
- cron/services: forbidden — contract disallows; if ever needed, must go through installer module with idempotent uninstall record.

Shutdown sequencing with deadlines:
1. t=0: signal intent; stop admitting new work.
2. Drain phase (deadline D1): in-flight tasks finish or checkpoint.
3. Release phase (deadline D2): guards dropped in reverse-acquisition order (LIFO) — deterministic teardown ordering matters for dependencies (e.g., unmount before deleting backing file).
4. Reap phase (deadline D3): kill process groups, wait with timeout, escalate SIGTERM→SIGKILL.
5. Verify (D4): probe ground truth; diff vs ledger; if empty → write receipt {hash, ts}; else → write incident record + attempt janitor pass once more; never hang: total budget T_shutdown (e.g., 10s soft, 30s hard), after which supervisor SIGKILLs the whole cgroup and janitor finishes cleanup next boot — and crucially the *supervisor* is designed so its own death still triggers kernel-side reclamation (cgroup removal by parent, pdeathsig chain).

Key insight to state: you can't make userspace reliable against SIGKILL, so push as much reclamation as possible into kernel-enforced constructs that die with the process/cgroup automatically (cgroups, pdeathsig, O_TMPFILE/unlinked files, memfd, abstract sockets, job objects, close-on-exec), and everything that can't be kernel-reclaimed gets a lease+reaper+journal so it's bounded-staleness instead of permanent.

Classification: three tiers of footprint:
- Tier 0 (kernel-reclaimed): memory, fds, threads, memfd, pipes, abstract sockets, cgroup-local processes (die when cgroup removed by parent), job-object children. Requirement: prefer these; nothing to leak even on -9.
- Tier 1 (leased): named kernel artifacts (pinned bpf, nft tables, TUN devices, mounted dirs, named sems/shm, unix socket files, pidfiles, tmp files with names, distributed locks). Auto-reclaimed by lease expiry + janitor; max staleness bounded (lease TTL ≤ 60s, janitor interval ≤ 30s ⇒ residue lifetime ≤ ~90s after death, and ≤0 on graceful path).
- Tier 2 (persistent-by-design): config, logs, user data — declared in contract, versioned, with explicit `uninstall --purge`. Never implicit. Must be listed by `ghost footprint ls --all`.

Blocking-call rules ("no wedged discovery"):
- Control plane commands (anything an operator runs) must complete ≤ N seconds or print partial results + exit code PARTIAL(=3?). Define exit codes: 0 ok, 1 error, 2 usage, 3 partial/degraded.
- No syscall without timeout in control paths: connect/send/recv timeouts, lock attempts use trylock-with-deadline, file IO on local disk only (no NFS on control path), subprocesses get WaitDelay.
- Internal locks: lock ordering registry, no IO under lock, watchdog thread detects any critical-section > 500ms and dumps + aborts (fail-stop beats wedged).
- Watchdogs: main loop heartbeat; if stalled > W, supervisor escalates: dump stacks → SIGABRT (core) → cgroup kill → janitor next start.

Ledger schema (concrete):
```
record Acquire {
  seq u64, ts, actor (component@pid+boot_id),
  kind: enum {PROC_GROUP, PORT, TMPDIR, FILE, SHM, SEM, UNIX_SOCK, BPF_PIN, NFT_TABLE, TUN, MOUNT, LOOP, LOCK_DIST, LOCK_FILE},
  key string,            // canonical identity (path/name/port#...)
  lease_ttl_ms u32,
  contract_ref string,   // which manifest line authorized it
  prev_hash, hash        // hash chain
}
record Release { seq, ts, acq_seq, how: DROP|EXPLICIT|REAPED }
```
Journal fsync'd with `O_DSYNC` directory sync; ring-buffered with compaction on clean shutdown.

Reconciliation algorithm (janitor at boot + every 30s):
```
live = union(probe(k) for k in classes)
owned = ledger.open_leases()           // not released, issuer boot_id != current OR expired
for item in live - owned: mark DRIFT    // exists but nobody claims -> candidate; require 2 consecutive observations before destroy unless unsafe (then quarantine)
for item in owned - live: mark RELEASED_GHOST (close lease)
for item in owned ∩ live where lease.expired or boot_id stale: REAP (destroy), log
DRIFT items older than grace: quarantine dir/quarantine namespace + alert; never silently delete unknown things (operator trust) except within our reserved namespaces where we're sole owner by construction (prefix ownership makes this safe).
```

Prefix-ownership rule: everything we create lives under reserved namespaces we provably own (paths `/var/lib/ghost/...`, names `gh*`, nft table `ghost_*`, bpf pin dir, cgroup `ghost.slice`, ports from contracted ranges). Then "unknown thing in our namespace" = ours by construction, safe to reap after grace. That kills the ambiguity problem.

Contract schema sketch:
```yaml
contract: v1
component: scheduler
process_groups: {max: 4, pattern: "gh-sched-*"}
ports: [{range: [21000,21100], proto: tcp}]
tmp: {root: "/var/lib/ghost/tmp", bytes: 1GiB}
kernel:
  bpf: {pin_dir: "/sys/fs/bpf/ghost/scheduler", max_progs: 8}
  nft_tables: ["ghost_sched"]
  tun_devices: {max: 2, pattern: "gh0-sched-*"}
blocking_budget_ms: {shutdown_total: 10000, cmd_default: 5000}
forbidden: [cron, systemd_units, mounts_outside_state_root, setuid]
```
Admission: loader validates contract against cluster policy; registrar refuses acquisitions without matching contract_ref; lint/static check rejects direct `std::process::Command`/`openat` outside wrapper (via import bans + code review gate + optional eBPF-based runtime audit in dev builds).

Kill-matrix testing (this is the heart of anti-boatmurdered verification):
